Renewal & Expansion Check-in 













































Renewal & Expansion Check-in  Crestline Bank
next_steps: Send updated Dedicated + EU region pricing and contract term options
Schedule capacity planning workshop with Crestline infra team
Share SOC 2 and ISO docs + network architecture checklist
Run 72-hr benchmark in eu-west region and share results
action_items: Jamie Park: Send updated pricing for Dedicated with EU region option by 2027-02-12
Sandeep Rao: Schedule capacity planning workshop and invite Crestline infra by 2027-02-15

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Sandeep Rao (Redwood SE), Maria Lopez (Crestline Head of AI), Ken Baxter (Crestline Infra), Priya Sharma (Crestline Procurement)

Summary: Quick renewal check-in, customer interested in upgrading dedicated capacity, adding EU region for data residency, and extending contract term for 12-24 months. Discussed latency/cost tradeoffs, VPC/private options, and next-step benchmarks.

Topics: renewal, capacity upgrade, additional regions (EU), contract extension, compliance docs

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Maria, thanks for making time - we wanted to run through your renewal and the expansion asks you shared last week.
[00:12] Maria Lopez: Yeah thanks Jamie, appreciate it. We've been generally happy, but the usage has grown faster than expected so we need to talk Dedicated capacity and also adding an EU region because a bunch of new customers are EU-based and legal wants data residency.
[00:24] Sandeep Rao: Morning Maria. Quick question - when you say "grow faster", do you mean peak concurrent requests, tokens per hour, or both? That helps figure out autoscale vs reserved sizing.
[00:36] Maria Lopez: Mostly tokens/hour, bump in embeddings, and a few large batch jobs overnight. Peak concurrent requests is still modest but those batch jobs spike memory usage.
[00:48] Ken Baxter: And for infra folks, the thing we care about is predictable throughput - we can't get surprise throttles during market opens. We ran into a couple of throttling events last month.
[00:58] Jamie Park: Right; so on Dedicated we can lock in baseline capacity and add burst. We also have fast failover to fallback models if a burst hits limits, but I want to go through numbers. Maria, do you have the typical and peak token numbers?
[01:12] Maria Lopez: I pulled rough numbers - avg tokens/hour is around 1.2M, peak about 6.5M during busy windows. Embeddings monthly about 30M vectors.
[01:24] Sandeep Rao: Ok good. For 6.5M peak we'd recommend a Dedicated pool with two p8d-style instances or equivalent with our throughput profile, plus autoscale headroom. That maps to the pricing Jamie will share.
[01:38] Priya Sharma: From procurement side, we also want to discuss contract length. A 12-month commitment seems ok but if we go 24 months we want better unit pricing and an option to add EU region later without a big uplift.
[01:52] Jamie Park: Totally reasonable. We typically offer step discounts for 12 vs 24 month commits, and for multi-region reservations we can provide a blended rate. I'll include both 12 and 24 month term tables in the pricing doc.
[02:04] Ken Baxter: On the EU region - we need VPC peering and KMS integration. Also audit logs retention is a must for the regulators.
[02:14] Sandeep Rao: We support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations for Private deployments and KMS for Dedicated via the control plane; I'll call out the differences. Audit logs retention is configurable via Redwood Console; default is 90 days but we can extend for enterprise add-on.
[02:28] Maria Lopez: Is there any impact on latency if we route EU traffic to eu-west Dedicated? Right now we run everything in US, and EU customers have a couple hundred ms added.
[02:40] Sandeep Rao: Routing to eu-west Dedicated will reduce round trip for EU users - typically you'll see latency drop by 80-120ms depending on model and network. We do need to set up prefix cache warmers in the EU pool to avoid cold starts for KV cache on first spikes.
[02:56] Jamie Park: Also worth noting, some higher entropy models with large context windows will have slightly higher inference time, but the regional placement still gives net latency savings for EU users.
[03:08] Priya Sharma: On the security checklist, procurement asked for SOC 2, ISO27001, SAML SSO, RBAC, and SOC 2 Type II evidence. You mentioned earlier you have SOC 2 - can you share the report?
[03:20] Jamie Park: Yes we can share SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation under an NDA. I'll add that to the doc share. We'll also include SSO/SAML guide and RBAC role examples from the Console.
[03:32] Maria Lopez: Great. A follow-up on billing: if we add EU region do tokens count separately per region or are they aggregated? And how do you handle egress between regions?
[03:44] Jamie Park: Billing is aggregated to the account, but for committed Dedicated pools we bill by reserved capacity per region if you have separate reservations. Egress between regions is measured and billed; we'll show examples in the pricing scenarios. I'll make sure to include a blended example for the 24-month scenario.
[03:58] Ken Baxter: We need tight SLOs. Are there SLA credits for latency or is it only uptime?
[04:06] Sandeep Rao: Our Dedicated offering includes SLA for uptime and best-effort latency SLOs; for stricter latency guarantees we recommend adding reserved headroom and multi-region failover. We can codify expected p95 ranges in the SLO appendix of the contract.
[04:22] Maria Lopez: On fallbacks - last month when the fleet got taxed there was a switch to a smaller model and we noticed quality regression. Can you control the fallback model family to preserve quality?
[04:34] Sandeep Rao: Yes, you can pin fallback policies to certain model variants. We can provide a canary rollout where fallback maintains the same family with slightly reduced context or quantized profile to preserve intent. We'll include recommended fallback policies in the runbook.
[04:50] Jamie Park: One operational thing - we propose a 72-hour benchmark in eu-west with a replay of your peak traffic. That will surface any memory or KV cache cold-start issues. We can run that before renewals are signed so you have objective numbers.
[05:02] Maria Lopez: That would be perfect. Also can we include a test for batch embedding jobs - they are the ones spiking memory.
[05:10] Sandeep Rao: Absolutely, we'll mirror both realtime and batch workflows. We'll also instrument token-level latency and cost breakdowns in the Console so you can see per-route economics.
[05:20] Priya Sharma: Procurement: if we want to extend to 24 months, what does the termination clause look like for a region we haven't enabled yet? We want flexibility.
[05:30] Jamie Park: We can do a clause that allows you to enable reserved capacity in a new region within the term at pre-agreed pricing tiers, with a limited uplift if volumes are small. We'll draft language and share.
[05:42] Ken Baxter: One more networking question - do you support private on-prem connector or only VPC peering?
[05:50] Sandeep Rao: For Private deployments we support on-prem packages and private control plane options; for Dedicated we support VPC peering and private endpoints. If you need an air-gapped deployment that's more of a Private engagement and we can scope that separately.
[06:04] Maria Lopez: Ok good. Let's talk numbers briefly - Jamie, you said you'd share pricing but can you give a ballpark on uplift for EU region and dedicated pool for our peaks?
[06:14] Jamie Park: Ballpark, adding an EU dedicated pool and two instances sized for your peak is roughly a 35-45% uplift over your current hosted spend, depending on commit term. The 24-month commit moves that down to about 20-30% uplift. I'll put precise numbers in the spreadsheet.
[06:28] Maria Lopez: Sounds reasonable, we just need predictability.
[06:32] Sandeep Rao: A comment on model quantization - for batch embedding jobs we can recommend int8 quant profiles to reduce memory, with minimal quality loss. We'll propose quantization profiles per workload in the Optimize recommendations.
[06:46] Priya Sharma: From procurement, SLA credits and legal redlines - we'll expect a standard enterprise DR appendix and data processing addendum.
[06:56] Jamie Park: Yep, we'll include a DPA and DR appendix. We'll also provide a sample exhibit for audit access.
[07:06] Maria Lopez: Great. A couple of quick operational asks - can we have a named CSM for day-to-day escalation if we go Dedicated?
[07:14] Jamie Park: Yes, CSM assignment is included for Dedicated customers. I'll note that and include the CSM ramp plan in the doc.
[07:22] Ken Baxter: For the benchmark, what telemetry do you need from our side?
[07:28] Sandeep Rao: We'll need replay logs, representative prompts and embedding payloads, peak timeline, and any auth/networking constraints for the eu-west region. Maria, if you can share those two weeks before the test that gives us time to set up warmers.
[07:40] Maria Lopez: I can get those over. I'll coordinate with Ken.
[07:44] Jamie Park: Ok to recap the action items...
[07:48] Jamie Park: Jamie: send updated pricing and 12/24 term tables, include blended EU examples and SLA appendix.
[07:55] Sandeep Rao: Sandeep: schedule capacity workshop and plan benchmark tests; prepare quantization and fallback policy recommendations.
[08:01] Maria Lopez: Maria: share traffic replay, peak metrics, and compliance contact for SOC2 NDA.
[08:08] Priya Sharma: Priya: I'll review contract templates and flag procurement must-haves.
[08:14] Jamie Park: Next meeting - let's tentatively schedule a capacity workshop the week of Feb 15, and I'll follow up with calendar invites after sending the pricing.
[08:22] Maria Lopez: Works for me. Thanks everyone.
[08:25] Ken Baxter: Thanks.
[08:26] Priya Sharma: Thanks all.

Meeting end.

References / shared artifacts:
- Pricing spreadsheet link: (shared in chat) "Redwood_Crestline_PRICING_v2.xlsx"
- SOC2/ISO docs: to be shared under NDA
- Benchmark plan doc: "crestline-eu-benchmark-plan.md"

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms (KMS sometimes transcribed as K-M-S), and model names abbreviated. Speaker labels mostly correct but we saw minor overlaps.
